title: Adaptive bandwidth-aware ingress mediator for dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Tenants on Dedicated fleets sometimes cause transient headroom exhaustion and produce prolonged recovery cycles when naive rate-limiting or simple token-bucket strategies are applied. This leads to SLO violations for latency-sensitive customers and underutilized burst windows for best-effort traffic.

Goal: Design and implement an "ingress mediator" that performs bandwidth-aware admission control across dedicated pools. The mediator should: (1) enforce tenant-level sustained throughput guarantees, (2) allow controlled short-term bursts, (3) softly shed or defer work when capacity is constrained, and (4) integrate with the autoscaler and console metrics for observability and policy tuning.

Scope: routing/admission layer only (not model runtime). Components: per-tenant entitlement tracker, adaptive bandwidth estimator, short-burst reservoir (burstpool), spill-to-secondary-routing for best-effort traffic, and a soft-recovery protocol that ramps resumed tenants to their baseline rather than instantly consuming headroom.

Non-goals: full fairness re-architecture, billing changes, or on-prem network changes.

Why different: instead of hard priority lanes or fixed-size token windows, the mediator uses a bandwidth estimator that combines long-term entitlement with short-term arrival patterns and hardware occupancy signals to decide admission and shedding with conservative recovery to avoid oscillation.
acceptance_criteria: Mediator enforces per-tenant sustained throughput within +/-10% of entitlement under steady load in lab tests.
Short-burst requests are allowed up to configured burstpool capacity and evicted predictably when fleet utilization exceeds 85%.
When shedding occurs, latency-sensitive SLO-tagged requests should be favored; console shows per-tenant shed metrics and reasons.
Autoscaler hooks receive a synthetic "pressure" signal from the mediator and trigger scale events in staging with correct cooldown behavior.
Rollout plan validated in Canary: 5% traffic for 48h, metrics show no increased P99 tail > 15% compared to control.
Design doc, test plan, and at least one implementation PR merge are present before wider rollout.
E2E regressions tests cover recovery ramp (soft-resume) and spill-to-secondary-routing behavior.
design_decisions: Admission model: hybrid quota + short-burst reservoir. Use a small long-window quota (60s) rather than per-second tokens to tolerate burstiness.
Bandwidth estimator: exponential moving average biased to slower decay (alpha=0.15) to avoid rapid oscillation from short spikes.
Shedding policy: staged soft-shed (defer -> prioritized drop -> hard drop) with tenant-level grace credits accrued during low-util periods.
Autoscaler integration: mediator emits a normalized pressure metric (0..1) that maps to existing autoscaler policies; autoscaler remains the source of truth for capacity changes.
Observability: expose per-tenant entitlements, current usage, burstpool consumption, and last-shed-reason to Console and internal dashboards.
Safety: default to conservative behavior if mediator loses connectivity to fleet occupancy signals (fallback to fixed-rate limiter).
tasks: Write design doc and sequence diagrams (confluence link below).
Implement entitlement tracker in admission-service (server-side), add bandwidth estimator module.
Create burstpool manager that allocates and reclaims burst credits across tenants.
Add telemetry / metrics and Console dashboard panels for mediator signals.
Hook mediator pressure metric into autoscaler test pipeline and staging clusters.
Canary rollout plan and runbook for rollback and mitigation.
Add regression tests: lab-sim harness for steady+burst scenarios and integration tests for spill-to-secondary routing.
notes: Initial spike showed stable behavior with alpha=0.15 and burstpool=20% of tenant entitlement in lab cluster (see PR bench notes).
We debated strict per-request tagging for SLO sensitivity vs. dynamic classification; settled on a header-based SLO tag with default 'latency-sensitive' class for chat/generation routes.
Planned feature: dynamic tenant hibernation is out of scope for this ticket but will be a follow-up if mediator proves stable.
